topics.label: Fossils
facts: Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from long ago, preserved in rock.
Most fossils form when an animal or plant is buried quickly in mud or sand.
Dinosaur bones are fossils that tell scientists about animals that lived millions of years ago.
Scientists who study fossils are called palaeontologists.

choices: The remains of a living thing from long ago, preserved in rock
questions.fact: Fossils are remains or traces of ancient living things, like bones or footprints in rock.

choices: A plant or animal is buried quickly in mud or sand
questions.fact: Quick burial protects remains from rotting, and minerals slowly replace them with stone.

questions.q: What do dinosaur bones tell scientists?
choices: About animals that lived millions of years ago
questions.fact: Dinosaur fossils show how these giant animals lived and what they looked like.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies fossils called?
questions.fact: Palaeontologists dig up and study fossils to learn about life long ago.

topics.label: Day and Night
facts: Day and night happen because Earth spins on its axis.
One full spin of Earth takes about 24 hours, which is one day.
When your part of Earth faces the Sun, it is daytime; when it faces away, it is night.
Earth's axis is tilted, which is why days are longer in summer and shorter in winter.

choices: The Sun turning on and off
questions.fact: Earth spins once every 24 hours, so each part takes turns facing the Sun.

questions.q: How long does one full spin of Earth take?
questions.fact: One spin takes about 24 hours, which is one day and one night.

questions.q: When is it daytime where you live?
choices: When your part of Earth faces the Sun
questions.fact: Daytime is when your side of Earth is turned towards the Sun.

questions.q: Why are summer days longer than winter days?
choices: The Moon is bigger in summer
The Sun is closer in summer
Earth's axis is tilted towards the Sun in summer
questions.fact: The tilt means the Sun stays above the horizon longer in summer.

topics.label: Plant Life Cycle
facts: A plant's life cycle is seed, germination, growth, flowering, and making new seeds.
Germination is when a seed starts to grow a root and a shoot.
Flowers are the part of the plant where seeds are made.
Pollination happens when pollen moves from one flower to another, which lets seeds form.

questions.q: What is the first stage of a plant's life cycle?
questions.fact: A plant's life starts as a seed, which holds a tiny baby plant inside.

choices: When a seed starts to grow
questions.fact: Germination is when a seed sprouts a root and a shoot.

questions.q: Which part of the plant makes seeds?
questions.fact: After pollination, the flower's ovary grows into a fruit with seeds inside.

choices: Pollen moving from one flower to another
questions.fact: Pollination lets flowers make seeds, often with help from bees.

topics.label: The Life Cycle of Animals
facts: A frog's life cycle starts as an egg, then a tadpole, then a young frog, then an adult frog.
A tadpole lives in water and breathes through gills, but an adult frog breathes with lungs and through its skin.
The change from a young animal into a very different adult is called metamorphosis.
Mammals, like dogs and humans, are born as babies that look like small versions of their parents.

questions.q: What is a baby frog called?
questions.fact: A baby frog is a tadpole, which lives in water.
Tadpoles live in water and breathe through gills.

choices: A change from a young animal into a very different adult
questions.fact: Metamorphosis is the big change from a young form, like a tadpole, into a different adult form.

questions.q: Which of these animals is born looking like a small version of its parent?
questions.fact: Mammals like dogs are born as babies that look like small versions of their parents.
